title: How many hours of HAZWOPER training does OSHA require?
description: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.120 HAZWOPER training: 40 or 24 hours initial, supervised field days, 8 hour annual refresher, supervisor and emergency responder levels.
shortAnswer: The Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) requires general site workers at hazardous waste cleanup sites to complete at least 40 hours of off site instruction and three days of supervised field experience under 29 CFR 1910.120(e). Occasional or low exposure workers need 24 hours and one day. On site managers and supervisors need the same initial training plus 8 hours of specialized training, and everyone needs 8 hours of refresher training annually.
keyTakeaways: HAZWOPER covers five operations: government mandated cleanups at uncontrolled hazardous waste sites, RCRA corrective actions, recognized voluntary cleanups, RCRA treatment, storage and disposal (TSD) facilities, and emergency response to hazardous substance releases.
Cleanup site workers need 40 hours off site plus three days of supervised field experience; occasional or fully characterized low exposure workers need 24 hours plus one day (1910.120(e)(3)).
On site managers and supervisors need the worker level training plus at least 8 additional hours of specialized training at job assignment (1910.120(e)(4)).
Cleanup site workers and supervisors need 8 hours of refresher training every year, including a critique of incidents from the past year (1910.120(e)(8)).
TSD facility employees need 24 hours initial and 8 hours annually under paragraph (p)(7); emergency responders are trained to defined levels under paragraph (q)(6).
jurisdiction: United States (federal): 29 CFR 1910.120 (general industry) and 29 CFR 1926.65 (construction), plus OSHA approved State Plans
regulator: Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), U.S. Department of Labor
appliesTo: Employers and employees at uncontrolled hazardous waste sites, including EPA National Priorities List sites
Contractors performing RCRA corrective action and recognized voluntary cleanups
Employees at RCRA treatment, storage and disposal facilities regulated under 40 CFR Parts 264 and 265
Employees who respond to releases or substantial threats of releases of hazardous substances
On site managers, supervisors and HAZWOPER trainers

sections.heading: Who does the HAZWOPER standard cover?

blocks.text: The Hazardous Waste Operations and Emergency Response (HAZWOPER) standard covers five kinds of operations, unless the employer can show the operation involves no employee exposure or reasonable possibility of exposure to safety or health hazards. Paragraph (a)(1) of [29 CFR 1910.120](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/subtitle-B/chapter-XVII/part-1910/subpart-H/section-1910.120) lists them.

items: Cleanup operations required by a governmental body at uncontrolled hazardous waste sites, including EPA National Priorities List sites, state priority lists and initial investigations of government identified sites.
Corrective actions involving cleanup at sites covered by the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act of 1976 (RCRA).
Voluntary cleanup operations at sites recognized by a governmental body as uncontrolled hazardous waste sites.
Operations involving hazardous wastes at treatment, storage and disposal (TSD) facilities regulated under 40 CFR Parts 264 and 265.
Emergency response operations for releases, or substantial threats of releases, of hazardous substances, without regard to location.

blocks.text: Each category has its own training paragraph: (e) for cleanup sites, (p)(7) and (p)(8) for TSD facilities, and (q)(6) for emergency response. The hour requirements quoted on this page are current as at November 2026. Picking the wrong paragraph is a frequent HAZWOPER training error, because the hour requirements differ sharply. Construction employers follow the parallel standard at 29 CFR 1926.65, and OSHA's [HAZWOPER standards page](https://www.osha.gov/hazardous-waste/standards) notes that State Plans must be at least as effective as federal OSHA and may set different or stricter requirements.

sections.heading: What initial training do cleanup site workers need?

blocks.text: General site workers need at least 40 hours of instruction off the site and at least three days of actual field experience under the direct supervision of a trained, experienced supervisor. Workers on site only occasionally for a limited task, or regularly on site in monitored areas below exposure limits, need at least 24 hours and one day.

blocks.text: Paragraph (e)(1)(ii) adds a gate: employees may not participate in or supervise field activities until they have been trained to the level their job function requires. Paragraph (e)(2) lists the topics the training must thoroughly cover, including the names of personnel responsible for site safety and health, site hazards, personal protective equipment, safe work practices, engineering controls, medical surveillance including signs of overexposure, and specified contents of the site safety and health plan.

sections.heading: What extra training do supervisors and trainers need?

blocks.text: On site managers and supervisors directly responsible for hazardous waste operations need the initial worker training and field experience plus at least eight additional hours of specialized training at the time of job assignment. Paragraph (e)(4) names example topics: the employer's safety and health program and associated training program, the personal protective equipment program, the spill containment program, and health hazard monitoring procedures and techniques.

Trainers must be qualified to instruct on the subject matter. Under paragraph (e)(5), they must have satisfactorily completed a training program for teaching the subjects, or hold the academic credentials and instructional experience necessary, and must demonstrate competent instructional skills and knowledge of the subject. A trainer file should therefore hold both subject credentials and evidence of instructional competence.

sections.heading: How are HAZWOPER certification and annual refresher training handled?

blocks.text: Employees and supervisors who complete the training and field experience must be certified by their instructor, or by the head instructor and trained supervisor, and given a written certificate. Anyone not certified, and without documented equivalent training, is prohibited from engaging in hazardous waste operations under paragraph (e)(6).

Paragraph (e)(8) requires eight hours of refresher training annually for cleanup site workers and for managers and supervisors. The refresher covers the (e)(2) and (e)(4) topics, any critique of incidents in the past year that can serve as training examples, and other relevant topics. The incident critique requirement means a refresher bought off the shelf every year without site specific content does not fully meet the rule.

Paragraph (e)(9) lets an employer skip initial training for an employee whose documented work experience or training is equivalent, and the employer must give the employee a copy of that documentation on request. Even then, employees new to a site must receive site specific training before entry and supervised field experience at the new site. Scheduling the annual cycle is covered in [how to set mandatory training refresh cycles](/guides/how-to-set-mandatory-training-refresh-cycles).

sections.heading: What training applies at TSD facilities and for emergency responders?

blocks.text: TSD facility employees exposed to health hazards or hazardous substances need 24 hours of initial training and 8 hours of refresher training annually under paragraph (p)(7), with a written certificate for initial training. Emergency responders are trained to the level of their role under paragraph (q)(6), with annual refresher training or a yearly demonstration of competency under (q)(8).

blocks.text: Under (q)(8)(ii), the employer must make a statement of the training or competency, and where a statement of competency is used instead of refresher training, must keep a record of the method used to demonstrate competency. Facilities that are also RCRA large quantity generators can count this emergency response training toward their RCRA program, as explained on the [EPA RCRA personnel training page](/regulations/epa-rcra-hazardous-waste-personnel-training).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry links each HAZWOPER role to its paragraph, tier and competencies, so a change in duties, such as a 24 hour worker starting to wear a respirator, flags the additional 16 hours and two field days automatically. Annual refresher content is linked to the incident records it must critique, which keeps the site specific element current.

faqs.q: Can HAZWOPER 40 hour training be completed entirely online?
faqs.a: The standard requires at least 40 hours of instruction off the site and at least three days of actual field experience under direct supervision of a trained, experienced supervisor. The field days cannot be delivered online, and paragraph (e)(2) topics such as personal protective equipment use are hard to evidence without hands on practice. Classroom hours delivered remotely should be checked against current OSHA interpretation.

faqs.q: What happens if a worker misses the annual 8 hour refresher?
faqs.a: Paragraph (e)(8) requires the refresher annually, and paragraph (e)(6) prohibits people who are not properly certified from engaging in hazardous waste operations. An employer should remove the worker from covered duties until the refresher is completed and record the gap and its closure, rather than allowing work to continue.

faqs.q: Do warehouse staff who might see a spill need HAZWOPER training?
faqs.a: Staff who might discover a release and will only notify others fall under the first responder awareness level in paragraph (q)(6)(i). Paragraph (q)(1) also exempts employers who evacuate employees from the danger area and do not permit them to assist, provided they have an emergency action plan under 29 CFR 1910.38. Staff who will contain a spill need operations level training or higher.

faqs.q: Is there a construction version of HAZWOPER?
faqs.a: Yes. Construction work is covered by 29 CFR 1926.65, which OSHA lists alongside 1910.120 on its HAZWOPER standards page. Employers in OSHA approved State Plan states must also check the state standard, which must be at least as effective as the federal rule and may differ.

(e)(3)(i) general site workers: minimum 40 hours off site and three days supervised field experience; (e)(3)(ii) and (iii): 24 hours and one day; (e)(3)(iv): additional 16 hours and two days
(e)(4) managers and supervisors: 40 hours and three days (or 24 hours and one day) plus at least eight additional hours of specialized training at job assignment
(e)(5) trainer qualifications; (e)(6) written certificate and prohibition for uncertified persons
(e)(8) eight hours refresher training annually including critique of incidents in the past year; (e)(9) equivalent training with site specific training for new sites
(p)(7) TSD employees: initial training 24 hours and refresher eight hours annually with written certificate

(q)(6): operations level at least eight hours; technician at least 24 hours; incident commander at least 24 hours; (q)(8) annual refresher or yearly competency demonstration with record of methodology
